Neha — thanks for the ping and the helpful summary. My read and proposed approach below.

Topline position: we should aim to be pragmatic on language, accept narrower transfer-impact mechanics, and push back on an open training carveout. Recommend a single consolidated redline we can send back rather than multiple one-off asks.

Suggested positions (high level):
1) Training carveout: propose an "explicit no-training-by-default" with an opt-in (or account-level paid option) for customers who want model training + a technical audit trail. That aligns with product and avoids accidental training of customer data.

2) Transfer impact addendum: Accept concept but limit triggers. Draft language: "Transfer Impact Addendum (TIA) only required where Redwood routes Customer Data to a non-EEA processing region for reasons other than Customer's explicit regional preference or Customer-paid failover extension; Redwood will provide at least 10 business days' notice and mitigation plan."

3) Liability: Push back on broad carveouts. Accept limited carveout language tied to documented failure of KMS or encryption controls but cap exposure consistent with MSA cap. Require evidence: SOC 2 Type II report + KMS cert (FIPS/HSM).

Execution plan: I'll draft a consolidated redline (RNW_DPA_proposed_redline.docx) capturing the above and mark optional language. Ben/Laura — flag anything operationally unachievable. I suggest routing the consolidated redline to Novus with a 1-page playbook and the Mutual Action Plan (MAP) to sync on timelines.

I'll attach the initial draft by EOD today.

-Karthik
